canonical_topic: Spot vs. forward natural gas price volatility and seasonality
definition: Forward natural gas prices follow a regular, predictable seasonal pattern, while spot prices move erratically because they reflect short-term, localized supply and demand shocks rather than a smooth seasonal curve.
core_idea: Because forward markets have time to arrange transportation and adjust supply, they trade in a smooth seasonal pattern; spot markets react instantly to whatever is happening right now, so they are much noisier and more volatile.
key_points: Forward prices show a regular, highly predictable seasonal trend.
Spot prices do not show the same seasonality and instead appear erratic.
Spot volatility tends to be higher than forward volatility.
relationships: Driven by the physical constraints on storing/transporting natural gas on short notice (see companion topic).
trading_implications: Risk models should not assume spot price behavior mirrors forward seasonality; spot exposure carries higher volatility risk than an equivalent forward position.
caveats: Assuming spot prices should track the same seasonal curve as forward prices.
